title: AI-SDLC HierarchyRoster v1
description: Roster of the named Claude Code sessions started by cli-hierarchy up, written to .ai-sdlc/dispatch/hierarchy.json. One entry per session. Tiers resolve the dispatch session or an idle executor from this file instead of hard-coded names.

schemaVersion.description: Roster schema version. Pinned so future readers can refuse rosters they do not understand.

project.description: Project the session belongs to: the repository basename unless cli-hierarchy up was given --project. Session names are qualified with it (<project>-<role>) so hierarchies of different projects on one machine do not collide. Optional for rosters written before project scoping; readers treat a missing value as the repository basename and the next up rewrites it. A mistake guard, not authentication.

name.description: Name the harness actually gave the session. Equals the requested name unless the harness added a collision suffix.

tmuxSession.description: tmux session hosting the agent. Equals the agent's requested name (one session per agent). Rosters written by the older single-session layout name 'ai-sdlc-hierarchy' and still validate. The schema only checks the shape; the tools additionally refuse to act on any entry whose session is not 'ai-sdlc-hierarchy' or a default hierarchy name equal to its window.

tmuxWindow.description: tmux window name. Always the name that was requested, so a later up can recognise its own window. Equals tmuxSession in the one-session-per-agent layout.

paneId.description: tmux pane id (for example '%14'). Empty string when it could not be read.

pid.description: Process id of the session as reported by the harness registry, or of the tmux pane when the registry had not yet listed the session. 0 when unknown.

model.description: Model the session was started with.

permissionMode.description: Permission mode the session was started with.

startedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the window was created.

status.description: 'starting' until the harness registry confirmed the session and its final name, then 'running'.
